stem: An applicant for a Massachusetts pharmacy technician licence is 19, holds a high school diploma, is of good moral character and has no drug-related felony. Which of the following, standing alone, satisfies the remaining eligibility requirement? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Certification conferred by a Board-approved certifying body.
A substantially equivalent pharmacy technician licence in good standing in another state.
A Board-approved passing score on a Board-approved assessment examination taken after completing a Board-approved training program.
Twelve months of employment as a pharmacy cashier in a licensed pharmacy.
A letter from the employing Manager of Record attesting to the applicant's competence.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 8.02(3)(e) sets out three alternative routes: certification by a Board-approved certifying body, a substantially equivalent out-of-state licence in good standing, or a Board-approved passing score on a Board-approved assessment examination taken after either a Board-approved training program or a minimum of 500 hours as a pharmacy technician trainee. They are alternatives, and none of them is an employer attestation of general competence.

choice_analysis.A: Correct: certification by a Board-approved certifying body is a complete route.
choice_analysis.B: Correct: a substantially equivalent out-of-state licence in good standing is a complete route.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: the examination route is complete once its training prerequisite is satisfied.
choice_analysis.D: Cashier employment is not pharmacy technician trainee experience and satisfies no route.
choice_analysis.E: An employer letter of competence is not one of the routes.

related_facts: The 500-hour trainee alternative must be attested under the pains and penalties of perjury and witnessed by the employer.
explanation.mpje_trap: The routes are alternatives, so satisfying one is enough, but an employer attestation is not among them.

reasoning_steps: Confirm the age, education, character and felony conditions are already met
Treat the three statutory routes as alternatives rather than cumulative
Reject proposals that substitute employer attestation for a stated route
